verdict.reasoning: Patient states symptoms have been going on for "just under a week" and describes burning/stinging when passing urine: "it's been going on for about just under a week" and "I notice a sort of burning, stinging, when I when I go to the toilet" (dysuria).
Patient reports increased urinary frequency: "I'm going to the toilet a lot more" and "I'm just like constantly looking for the toilet."
Patient describes lower abdominal (suprapubic) aching pain worse with voiding: "it's kind of at the bottom of my tummy... mainly when I go to the loo... an achey pain I suppose."
Patient notes pink urine today: "I think, well today I noticed, um, that it was like a bit pink. The, the urine."

Patient denies nausea/vomiting and fevers, and denies pain moving to back/sides: "No, no nausea vomiting"; "Um no, no not that I've noticed" (re fevers); "And does the pain move anywhere else? ..." Patient: "No, no, no."

Patient reports longstanding IBS with variable stool frequency and consistency: "I think I have, um, IBS... I just kinda pass, uh, my bowels like quite, quite a lot" and "sometimes it's a bit softer, sometimes it's a bit... harder and kind of hard to predict," and confirms no new bowel symptoms.
Sexual activity with long-term partner and combined OCP use are documented: "I have a, a long-term, um, boyfriend" and "Uh yeah, uh I'm um on the pill... combined pill."
Patient reports not really using condoms with boyfriend and LMP 2 weeks ago: "I don't really use condoms with my boyfriend" and "Um, two weeks ago" in response to "when was your last period?"
Patient denies abnormal vaginal discharge: "have you noticed any other discharge... ?" Patient: "Hmm no I don't think so. Nothing unusual."
IBS is explicitly mentioned: "I think I have, um, IBS" and later doctor: "in terms of your health otherwise... apart from the IBS".
Patient uses combined oral contraceptive pills: "Uh yeah, uh I'm um on the pill" and clarifies "combined pill."

Patient takes an IBS medication starting with M for cramps: "I take, um, something for the IBS as well. Um it begins with an M" and doctor confirms the name; then: "And is that for the cramps, the crampy pain?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah."
Patient reports allergy to clindamycin: "there was an antibiotic, um, called Clindamycin... that didn't, go too well, with me" and doctor: "OK, OK, OK... I'll make a note of that."
No family history of bladder or kidney problems: Doctor asks, "any history of problems with the bladder or the kidneys?" Patient: "No, no."
Patient is a university student studying English: "what are you studying at university?" Patient: "I'm studying, uh, English."
Patient lives in halls with a flatmate: "I am living in halls at the moment, uh at uni... I'm just living with a flatmate I suppose."
Patient occasionally consumes alcohol: "I drink occasionally, um, kind of socially, um, with friends."
Cannabis tried once about 1.5 weeks ago: "I smoked weed for the first time. Uh, like a week and a half ago."
Patient is a non-smoker: "I tried weed for the first time... but, uh, I don't smoke."

Doctor diagnoses likely simple UTI/cystitis and symptoms match: "I think it's, um, probably just a simple what we'd say a UTI or a cystitis, bladder infection" and patient has dysuria, frequency, suprapubic ache, and pink urine as documented earlier.
Clindamycin allergy is acknowledged and relevant: patient reports allergy to clindamycin and doctor says, "I'll make a note of that," which supports including it in assessment.

Single cannabis trial and counseling occurred: patient admits first-time weed use "a week and a half ago"; doctor responds with advice against ongoing use: "I do strongly advise you..." and later "I would strongly recommend you, you know, to avoid if you can."

Doctor plans empiric antibiotics nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim: "we've got a choice of two antibiotics something called Trimethoprim or, Nitrofurantoin which is a three day course" and describes treating the UTI.

Urine sample plan is explicit: "It's probably worth giving us a urine sample today as well if you can, so we can send it off to the lab" and later details coming in to drop off a sample for testing and results follow-up.
Hydration advice given: "make sure you're well hydrated, drink plenty of fluids."
Doctor recommends simple paracetamol but does not state it was prescribed: "If you are having some pain, simple Paracetamol, um, would probably be advisable." The word "prescribed" is not used.

Safety-net advice given: "do bear in mind those symptoms I mentioned about the fever and the back pain and vomiting. If you have any of those give me a call" and "if it is indeed positive... if things still are still not getting any better next week come back and see me."
While clindamycin allergy is noted, there is no explicit advice recorded to avoid clindamycin: doctor says only "I'll make a note of that" without specific avoidance counseling.
Doctor advises avoiding ongoing cannabis use: "I do strongly advise you to you know..." (in context of weed) and later "I would strongly recommend you, you know, to avoid if you can."
